chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no liability (guarantee) for the borrowed item (ariyyah) except if one has stipulated a guarantee for it, except for the dinars, for they are guaranteed even if no guarantee was stipulated for them.'

key_terms.الدَّنَانِير: Gold dinars, used here as a metonym for currency/money.
key_terms.ضَمَان: Liability or guarantee for loss or damage.
key_terms.عَارِيَّة: A gratuitous loan of an item for use, where the item is returned in kind.

ai.seo_question: Is a borrower liable for damage to a borrowed item in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between 'ariyyah' (gratuitous loan) and qard (loan of value), ruling that dinars are always guaranteed due to their nature as currency, whereas other items are only liable if a guarantee was explicitly stipulated. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that currency retains its value and is consumed by use, necessitating strict liability to ensure fairness in financial transactions. The exception highlights the unique status of dinars as a medium of exchange where loss equates to consumption of value.
